# Read-Back

A touring band's one-nighter load-in at The Lyric venue is being coordinated by a house crew of eight, starting at 8 AM and finishing by doors (show time). The schedule chains two truck deliveries through a single loading dock: lighting truck (60 min) must fully unload before the backline truck (45 min) can enter, then the dock must be cleared (15 min). Once unloaded, lighting rigs bars on stage (45 min), focuses from the desk (60 min), and builds cues (30–90 min variable, depending on plot cleanliness); PA flies concurrently (75 min) and rings out the house (20 min); monitors set up after backline truck clears (45 min) and ring out wedges (20 min). Backline goes on stage only after the dock is fully clear (45 min), and soundcheck happens only when *both* house and wedges are rung out (60 min). The band then has dinner in the green room (60 min), while front-of-house is set from two hours before doors (60 min), the house is cleaned (30 min), and doors open with a 30-minute walk-up. The show runs as long as it runs, then backline strikes 15 minutes after the show ends (45 min on the dock). The critical bottlenecks are the single loading dock (no parallel truck unloading) and the single stage (no overlapping setup work), plus the single lighting desk (focus and cue-build are sequential), and soundcheck's dependency on two completed departments.
